chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Zurara and Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who said, 'I am in the state of Ihram for Hajj if I do not do such and such,' and he did not do it, he (the Imam) said, 'It is of no consequence.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: It is of no consequence / not binding
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a conditional vow made during Hajj if the condition is not fulfilled?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of conditional vows (ayman) made by a pilgrim in the state of Ihram, ruling that if the specified condition is not fulfilled, the vow is not binding ('laysa bi-shay'). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that conditional vows are contingent upon the actual occurrence of the condition, preventing unnecessary religious burden on the individual. It serves as a practical guideline for pilgrims to understand the flexibility of their vows during the sacred rites of Hajj.
